judged_text: Confusable-pair binding: the EventManager is constructed from the REQUESTING user (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, `...user`) instead of the booking organizer (`booking.userId`), even though the code explicitly resolved `organizer` as a separate record. When an attendee or team admin (not the organizer) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with the caller's calendar credentials against the organizer's booking — the calendar update targets the wrong account's calendars, fails outright for users with no calendar credential, or mutates via credentials that don't own the event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code resolves `organizer` (via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId } ... })`) but then constructs `EventManager` using the requesting user context: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. This means when a non-organizer (attendee/team admin) invokes `addGuests`, the calendar update will run under the caller’s credentials rather than the booking organizer’s, which can target the wrong calendar account or fail if the caller lacks credentials. This behavior is directly evidenced by the diff.
